Claude responded: Activating a lesson takes four steps.

Registering a new lesson within the content system.
Registering a new lesson within the content system.

Activating a lesson takes four steps. The first two are the ones that make it playable.

1. Check the lesson’s id

Open src/data/lessons/lesson-1-2.js and make sure the top of the object says:

js
export default {
  id: '1.2',
  title: 'Anatomy of a control system',
  ...

The id must exactly match the lesson id in src/data/units.js ('1.2', as a string). A mismatch is the most common reason a lesson stays “coming soon”.

2. Register it in src/data/lessons/index.js

Add an import and add the lesson to the list:

js
import lesson11 from './lesson-1-1.js';
import lesson12 from './lesson-1-2.js';   // new
import lesson21 from './lesson-2-1.js';
import lesson22 from './lesson-2-2.js';

const all = [lesson11, lesson12, lesson21, lesson22];   // lesson12 added

export const lessons = Object.fromEntries(all.map((l) => [l.id, l]));

Keep the .js at the end of each import path. Save, and the “coming soon” circle for 1.2 becomes playable. It unlocks once you finish 1.1.

3. Check it for mistakes

If you added the week 1 scripts, run:

npm run validate

It lists problems in plain English, such as an answer pointing outside the options, duplicate drag items, or too many questions. While npm run dev is running, mistakes also show as a red page.

4. Register it in Supabase (only if you ran migration 002)

If you ran 002_valid_lessons.sql, the database rejects XP for lessons it doesn’t know about. Run:

npm run sync-lessons

Copy the SQL it prints, paste it into Supabase’s SQL Editor, and click Run. Without this step the lesson works, but its XP never reaches the leaderboard, and the browser console says “Lesson 1.2 is not registered in Supabase yet”.

Quick checks if it doesn’t appear

ProblemLikely cause
Still “coming soon”Not added to all in index.js, or the id doesn’t match units.js
Red error pageA content mistake. Read the first line, which names the question
LockedFinish lesson 1.1 first, since lessons play in order
Blank pageA missing comma or bracket in the lesson file. The terminal shows the line number

Unit 2 will stay locked until 1.3, 1.4 and 1.5 are also written, because a unit only unlocks when every lesson in the one before it is finished.

If you hit an error, paste it along with the top of your lesson-1-2.js and I’ll fix it.

Claude responded: A blank page almost always means the browser hit an error and stopped drawing.

Listing likely error messages and their matching causes
Listing likely error messages and their matching causes

A blank page almost always means the browser hit an error and stopped drawing. The error is shown in two places, so check both before changing anything.

Step 1: find the error (30 seconds)

  1. Terminal: look at the window running npm run dev. Red text there means a code or import problem, and it names the file and line.
  2. Browser: press F12 (Cmd + Option + I on a Mac), open Console, and refresh. The first red line is the cause. Later errors are usually knock-on effects.

Step 2: match the message (running on localhost)

Since you’ve just added lesson 1-2, check those first:

MessageCauseFix
Failed to resolve import "./lesson-1-2.js"The file name or folder doesn’t match the importCheck the spelling and capitals in src/data/lessons/ and in index.js
Unexpected token, Expected ",", Unterminated stringA syntax slip in lesson-1-2.js: a missing comma, bracket or quote. The terminal shows the line numberFix that line, and look for a comma missing between two questions
does not provide an export named 'default'The lesson file has no export default { at the topAdd it
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'color')The lesson’s id doesn’t match units.js, so the intro screen crashesMake both say '1.2'
Failed to resolve import ... Wordmark or ... SoundToggleYou imported a file you haven’t createdCreate src/components/Wordmark.jsx or SoundToggle.jsx
Wordmark is not definedYou used the component without adding its import lineAdd the import at the top of that file
Invalid hook callHook lines sit outside a component (the ResultScreen mistake from earlier)Move them inside the function
No errors anywhere, still blankAn edit to main.jsx or index.html broke it (for example, the <div id="root"> line was removed)Compare both files with the versions I gave you

If you installed the week 1 changes, a content mistake shows as a red page listing the problems, so a plain white page points at a syntax error instead.

Step 3: if the blank page is on your VPS

This is a different set of causes. In the browser’s console, look for:

MessageCauseFix
Unexpected token '<'The server sent index.html where a JavaScript file was expected: a missing try_files line, or the /assets files are missingCheck the Caddyfile and that assets/ exists on the server
Files in the Network tab show 404You uploaded the wrong thing: the dist folder itself instead of its contents, or the source projectls /var/www/automation101 should show index.html and assets/ directly
403 errorsWrong file permissionssudo chown -R $USER /var/www/automation101
src/main.jsx is requestedYou uploaded the source index.html, not the built oneRun npm run build, then upload what’s in dist/
Page loads but the leaderboard is missingYou built without your .env fileRebuild on the machine that has .env
Old version still showsCached index.htmlHard-refresh, and check the Caddyfile caching lines

What I need to help further

  1. Is it localhost:5173 or your VPS?
  2. Paste the first red line from the browser console, plus anything red in the terminal.
  3. If it started after adding lesson 1-2, paste the top 15 lines of lesson-1-2.js and your src/data/lessons/index.js.

With those I can usually name the exact line.
